title: NeuroLM’s frozen features on arithmetic and rest
question: Do NeuroLM’s frozen EEG features separate rest from mental arithmetic better than band power?

placement.text: A separate panel on the pilot studies page, outside the pilot count and every leaderboard and model ranking; the core Arithmetic & rest matrix keeps its rows.

metric_units: balanced accuracy, macro-F1 and chance levels are proportions in [0,1], and paired differences are differences of proportions: multiply by 100 for percent or percentage points; dimensions and counts of people, recordings, windows, channels, folds, fits and resamples are whole numbers; null means not computed, never zero
scope: NeuroLM-B stays frozen. One fixed ridge head (alpha 100) is fitted on each of three representations of the same 2,160 two-second windows from 36 people, in five participant-held-out folds: 15 fits and no tuning. Scores are equal-person means; the paired differences carry participant-bootstrap intervals.

cohort.name: EEG During Mental Arithmetic Tasks
cohort.split: whole participants held out: participants sorted and assigned to a fold by index modulo five, so no person is in training and test of the same fold
cohort.labels: the recording condition in the file name, pre-task rest against serial subtraction; the participants’ count-quality groups are left unused

model.name: NeuroLM-B
model.paper_title: NeuroLM: A Universal Multi-task Foundation Model for Bridging the Gap between Language and EEG Signals
model.parameters_basis: a strict restore of the checkpoint, every state entry present and none unexpected
model.transfer: supervised: the frozen NeuroLM outputs feed a linear head trained on the other folds’ labels
model.weights_note: no weights are distributed; the SHA-256 identifies the checkpoint used and grants nothing

adapter.filter: Butterworth band-pass, applied forward and backward over the retained minute
adapter.demean: per channel in each two-second window
adapter.units: microvolts, divided by 100 for NeuroLM; band power uses the microvolt windows

probe.scaler: StandardScaler fitted on training windows only
probe.head: RidgeClassifier

arms.label: tokenizer features
arms.definition: the mean of NeuroLM-B’s 38 tokenizer hidden states per window (two one-second blocks of 19 channels), taken before its vocabulary projection

arms.label: band power
arms.definition: 95 absolute log band powers: 19 channels by 5 bands (1–4, 4–8, 8–13, 13–30 and 30–75 Hz), Welch with a one-second Hann window at 200 Hz on the same windows

arms.label: GPT hidden states
arms.definition: the mean of the 38 final normalised GPT hidden states from the same EEG-only forward pass, which stops before the language-model head

code.scope: NeuroLM’s source code at the pinned commit

checkpoint.as_stated_by: the licence tag in the Hugging Face repository metadata at the pinned revision

rights.summary: EEGMAT 1.0.0: Open Data Commons Attribution License 1.0 (Zyma et al., 2019; PhysioNet). NeuroLM code: MIT. NeuroLM-B checkpoint: CC BY 4.0 per its Hugging Face metadata; no weights distributed.

limitations.text: EEGMAT is NeuroLM’s Workload task, one of the six instruction tasks in its pinned code, and the training stage of this checkpoint is unresolved: its metadata (epoch 19, iteration 83,660, initialised from GPT-2, learning rate 0.0006) fits a pretraining checkpoint, and instruction tuning is unverified. The backbone may have seen these people, so exposure is shown as unknown.

This pilot has its own offline adapter: a fourth-order zero-phase Butterworth band-pass at 0.1–75 Hz, resampling from 500 to 200 Hz, per-window demeaning, microvolts divided by 100 for NeuroLM, and no notch filter, where NeuroLM’s own pipeline adds a 50/60 Hz notch. The core Arithmetic & rest protocol filters nothing and resamples to 250 Hz, so these scores have their own panel.

The band-power arm is 95 absolute log band powers (19 channels by 5 bands, 1–75 Hz, Welch at 200 Hz), a different feature set from the core matrix’s Spectral ridge row, which uses log relative spectra from 0.5–45 Hz at 250 Hz.
Rest is recorded before the task, so recording order moves with the label, and the pilot does not isolate cognitive workload.
The 95 band-power and 768 NeuroLM dimensions share one fixed alpha, which does not equalise capacity or effective regularisation.
There is no random-initialisation control, so the pilot says nothing about a causal benefit of pretraining.
Intervals come from 1,000 participant resamples of the 15 fixed fitted heads and exclude refit uncertainty. Each arm has a point estimate only.

EEGMAT is a known development cohort, used across this site. Predictions were sealed before scoring for procedural integrity: the labels are in the file names, and each person’s windows train the heads of the other folds.
The source README reports prior ICA cleaning of the published signals.

Frozen features with a supervised linear head: no text prompt, generated answer or language-model output entered any score, and nothing here measures instruction tuning, question answering, zero-shot use, cognitive workload, clinical use or online decoding.

audits.boundary: The independent audit refitted all 15 heads from the sealed NeuroLM and band-power values and reproduced every score and interval; the NeuroLM features themselves were not re-extracted by a second implementation.

release_record.decision: Publish the NeuroLM EEGMAT frozen-feature pilot as its approved aggregates: a separate panel on the pilot studies page, outside the pilot count and every leaderboard.
release_record.rights: EEGMAT keeps its released record: Open Data Commons Attribution License 1.0, aggregate results only. NeuroLM’s code is MIT at the pinned commit. The NeuroLM-B checkpoint is CC BY 4.0 as the licence tag of its Hugging Face repository states, and its 30-byte model card adds no terms. No weights are distributed, and no endorsement by NeuroLM’s authors is implied.
